title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Casus quartus, §§XVI–XIX): an elastic thread that is already curved in its unloaded state. Its natural curvature is 1/r(s), where s is arc length and r is the radius of osculation. A load deforms it to a curve with tangent angle φ(s). The planar equilibrium equations from the earlier sections are used, with T the tension along the tangent, V the transverse (shear) force, and Vv the bending moment (V times a lever arm v). Loads per unit length are p (tangential) and q (normal).
(I) dT = p ds − V dφ.
(II) T dφ = dV − q ds.
(III) d(Vv) = V ds, i.e. dM/ds = V.

§XVII, constitutive law: only the departure of the curvature from its natural value needs a moment. Euler therefore replaces dφ/ds by dφ/ds − 1/r in the elastic-moment law. With uniform stiffness A this gives M = Vv = A(κ − κ0), where κ = dφ/ds and κ0 = 1/r.

§XVIII: take ds constant and differentiate the moment law. Equation (III) then gives V = A(d²φ/ds² + r'/r²). It follows that v = M/V = r ds (r dφ − ds)/(r² ddφ + ds dr). (I) and (II) give two expressions for T, and comparing them yields the differential equation of the curve.

§XIX, circular natural shape (r = a): V = A φ''. The lever arm is v = (a dφ ds − ds²)/(a ddφ). Equation (I) integrates to T = ∫p ds − A φ'²/2. Equation (II) gives T = (A φ''' − q)/φ'.

Next page: the final equation does not contain a. The natural curvature enters only through integration constants, namely the end conditions on the moment Vv. In modern terms, for a uniform rod with constant intrinsic curvature the field equations equal those of a straight rod; κ0 appears only in the moment boundary conditions.
errors: The denominator of v in §XVIII is printed as r² ddφ − ds·dr; it should be r² ddφ + ds·dr. This follows from V = A(ddφ/ds² + dr/(r² ds)) = A(r² ddφ + ds dr)/(r² ds²). It is a sign slip, presumably typographical. The r = a specialisation is unaffected.
Minor: the integration T = ∫p ds − Aφ'²/2 silently absorbs the integration constant into ∫p ds. This is acceptable.

ideas.what: Moment of an initially curved elastic rod is proportional to the change of curvature: M = A(dφ/ds − 1/r)
ideas.modern_name: Linear constitutive law for rods with intrinsic (natural) curvature, M = EI(κ − κ0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler. The naturally curved lamina was already treated variationally in Additamentum I of the Methodus inveniendi (1744), and Jakob Bernoulli raised the question earlier.
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I; E410 itself; discussed by Truesdell in Opera omnia II.11 part 2

ideas.what: Shear force as derivative of bending moment, V = dM/ds, combined with tangential and normal force balances
ideas.modern_name: Planar Kirchhoff–Clebsch rod equilibrium equations with shear force
ideas.where_published: E410; Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies 1638–1788

ideas.what: For constant natural curvature, the intrinsic curvature drops out of the field equations and enters only through the end moment conditions
ideas.modern_name: Uniform intrinsic curvature as a boundary-condition effect, equivalent to a prestress or end moment
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in standard rod theory (e.g. Antman); Euler states it here

deep.surprise_reason: Standard content of a well-studied paper analysed at length by Truesdell. The only noteworthy points are a sign slip in the formula for v and the (known) remark that a uniform natural curvature affects only the boundary conditions.
transcription_corrections: Image shows dT = pds − Vdφ with a capital V, consistent with the transcription.
In §XIX the denominator in T = ∫pds − A·dφ²/(… ds²) should read 2ds²; the print is slightly ambiguous ('a' vs '2'), but 2 is mathematically correct.
'eequationes' in the print is a typo for 'aequationes'.
